top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a genuine new mechanism, the magic-wavelength trap that cancels the lattice light shift, and it has been reproduced and surpassed independently in several laboratories with comparisons agreeing near 10^-18. The credit allocation is clean, with both laureates named by every member who proposed laureates. The citation stays on the discovery and its realization, not on applications or the redefinition of the second. The result is mature, robust and already opens fundamental-physics tests, so it is clearly preferable to withholding the prize.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; optical lattice clocks lie outside my superconducting-circuit work and WACQT, and I have no listed connection to Katori or Ye
